best_parts: node gate_t30 and intub_t30a: feedback names the tempting model ('waiting is the tempting model'), refutes it with the trigger signs, then gives a sure_note for confident errors (hypercorrection path)
node intub: three-trigger probe for TR30 is a delayed re-test of the gate probe in a new form, so the same trap is met three times (gate, intub, final) before the segment ends
node final: cold probe with no help option and ask_confidence, so the segment closes on an unaided check
flaws: node intub: the correct option is the only one listing several signs and is the longest reply, so the key is findable by form
node final: the correct reply is the longest of the three ('Secure the airway now, before the swelling closes it'), a mild telegraph
node final_t30: 'Give fluids and watch; intubate if the airway closes' carries two errors (fluids first, and waiting), breaking one-error-per-option
node gate_hint: 'which one comes first' nearly gives the answer (A of ABCDE); the hint should point at risk, not order

best_parts: nodes t29 and t30: 'Show me why' / 'Why not wait for stridor?' agency routes to explain nodes, so a learner who doubts the feedback can ask for the reason
node p2: the airway-versus-TBSA contrast separates two TR29 surface forms (burn numbers first, fluid first) from the right order, a second form of the same trap
node ok: fast lane 'I am sure, skip the check' sits beside the primary probe, so experts are not forced through the whole segment
flaws: node ok: the skip lane goes to @next, which drops p2 and p3 entirely, so the early-intubation mechanism (p3) is never tested on the expert path
node p3_part: 'partial' option says 'Partly right' and returns to p3 with no credit and no different explanation; the hoarseness-proves-lung-injury model is weakly tempting
node p2 correct option is first in position and the longest, a mild telegraph
node t29b and t29c: no sure_note, unlike the other trap feedback in this segment, so confident errors here get no hypercorrection cue
node start: the TR30 trap is worded as 'intubate only if stridor appears' with the same model as p3, so the learner's diagnosis is shared across the two probes, lowering separation

best_parts: node gate_hint: 'what the burn sum can safely wait for' points at the reasoning without naming the answer, the best hint wording of the three
node end_recap: a short explain node that consolidates airway, intubation and secondary survey before the segment ends
node contrast_t29: 'Show me why' jumps to end_recap, which avoids repeating a feedback loop the learner has already seen
flaws: node teach: the intubation triggers are told before the learner is asked why, breaking ask-before-tell on the correct path
node early: only one trap option (TR30) plus the correct reply and help, so the probe offers one distractor and the key is easy to find
node contrast: one trap (TR29) plus correct and help, a binary-like probe with little diagnostic spread
no fast lane: every learner, including one who is sure, passes through gate_ok, teach, early and contrast, against the blueprint's skip-lane preference
node contrast_t29: no hint node on the path back before 'show me why', and the wrong-model name is not given

merge_ideas: a's gate, intub and final spine (three TR30 forms, sure_notes, cold final) with b's agency 'Why' routes on the trap feedback and b's skip lane that still tests the mechanism (route the skip to p3 instead of @next)
c's non-revealing hint wording ('what the burn sum can safely wait for') in place of a's gate_hint, and c's end_recap as the closing consolidation node after a's final_ok
give the early intubation trap two distractors of different forms (sign-based wait and distress-based wait) plus a partial, so the probe diagnoses as well as a's intub node
